attrs.evidence: governance/experiment_falsifiers.mjs v0.2.0 (16 cases) + run_state.mjs resolveState(); blind_run.mjs, holdout_score.mjs and holdout_runner.mjs all accept --state-root, and --complete refuses a summary whose state root is not the one the transition operates on. Falsifier O: SIGKILL mid-battery leaves governance/blind-run.json and receipts/ byte-identical. Falsifier Z: measured by digest over the live tree taken before the first case. Gate `gov-nest`.
attrs.statement: NEVER REWRITE THE ACTIVE EXPERIMENT RECORD TO PROVE THE ACTIVE EXPERIMENT RECORD CANNOT BE REWRITTEN INCORRECTLY. experiment_falsifiers.mjs v0.1.0 drove the LIVE governance/blind-run.json through every state and restored it in a `finally` -- and `make governance` invokes that battery. An external kill does not run `finally`: GPT's execution was interrupted by a resource limit and left an authoritative tree reading REVEALED with dryrun-a and dryrun-b as its subjects. Case Z, which asserts the restore, only runs when the process REACHES case Z, so the battery's own guarantee was conditional on nothing interrupting it -- and a SIGKILL, a CI timeout or a reboot during the real experiment would have left the real record in a synthetic state. THE STATE ROOT IS NOW INJECTABLE: every lifecycle program accepts --state-root, the battery copies the record into a temporary one and never opens the authoritative record for writing, and a measurement taken under a non-canonical root can only complete the run that lives beside it. Case Z became a measurement of an invariant rather than of a cleanup's success, and case O spawns the battery again, SIGKILLs it mid-flight, and digests the authoritative record afterwards -- an EXTERNAL INTERRUPTION, which is the thing no `finally` can be tested against from inside a process that completes.
